text:
This MV feels like a whole story about a fallen angel searching for love, freedom, and a place to belong. 🪽 At first, Jennie feels almost trapped in this beautiful fantasy world, surrounded by all these angelic and fairytale-like images, but underneath all the beauty there’s so much loneliness. The little girl with the wings feels like an important part of her journey, almost like the innocent side of herself that is still looking for somewhere safe to belong.

The scenes with the swans, the lake, the forest, the house, and Jennie underwater all feel like different parts of this dreamlike journey. It feels like she's slowly confronting things she has been trying to escape from. The water almost feels like she's being pulled deeper into her own emotions, while the angel imagery shows that even something that looks beautiful and perfect can still feel lost.

Then we see the couples and all the imagery surrounding love, which makes the lyrics hit even harder. She's surrounded by love but still feels alone, and that's what makes her “fall” feel less like becoming evil and more like losing the feeling of having somewhere to belong.

And the ending with the little girl, the burning house, and Jennie becoming surrounded by thorns is so heartbreaking. 🔥🌹 It feels like she finally stops running from everything and faces it. The thorns are painful, but they can also become roses, so maybe the pain and loneliness she's experienced are part of what allows her to become her true self.

I don't think the fallen angel is someone who needs to return to heaven. I think she's someone who had to fall in order to discover who she really is. And in the end, she finds freedom not by becoming perfect again, but by accepting herself. 🪽🌹

She longed for love, but to her it felt like a flickering light, because that hope was so fragile. The only moments of freedom and peace came when she could escape the cramped house, with its television endlessly broadcasting a toxic entertainment world. It is a truly beautiful video and a beautiful song.
But the story in this video has scenes that remind me of the horror films “INSIDIOUS” and “MIDSOMMAR.” (and “Illuminati”)

The red veils worn by the young girls look as if they are stained with blood, and they bring to mind baby angels with their heads cut off.

The child inside the burning house, surrounded by flames, is speaking as if she is about to cry, with a terrified, tearful expression.

Whatever Jennie intended, many people seem to feel the same way I do.

text: I honestly think people are looking way too deeply into the dark imagery and not enough into the actual lyrics. If you simply read the song, the meaning is pretty understandable. “Fallen angel” doesn’t automatically mean something demonic or related to the Illuminati. It can represent someone who feels lost, vulnerable, or like they’ve fallen away from where they belong. The whole song keeps coming back to not wanting to be left alone, searching for someone, and wanting to find a place that can become a home. Even the line about her wings being useless without someone shows that the “angel” imagery is being used emotionally, not literally. I think some people just aren’t used to seeing Jennie in this kind of vulnerable and melancholic concept, so they focus more on the visuals and immediately assume the worst instead of trying to understand what the song is actually saying. You don’t have to like the song or the MV, but calling it demonic just because it uses dark angel imagery feels like missing the point of the song itself.

text:
~~ FALLEN ANGEL de JENNIE~~

Aunque el MV tiene una estética oscura, fuego y escenas que pueden parecer perturbadoras, la historia no trata simplemente de que Jennie sea “la villana”.

La niña representa la inocencia y esa parte de nosotros que todavía cree en la libertad y en los sueños. Jennie aparece como un ángel que ha caído y comienza un viaje por diferentes emociones: el amor, la soledad, la búsqueda de un hogar y el dolor.

Las flores y las mariposas representan transformación, mientras que las grietas muestran cómo aquello que parecía perfecto puede romperse.

El fuego simboliza la destrucción y, al mismo tiempo, la transformación: dejar atrás una versión anterior de uno mismo. Por eso es tan importante la escena en la que Jennie se encuentra con la niña dentro de la casa en llamas. Puede interpretarse como un encuentro con su propia inocencia, con su “niña interior”.

La rosa entre las espinas resume gran parte del mensaje: el dolor y las dificultades también pueden formar parte de nuestro crecimiento y de aquello en lo que nos convertimos. 🌹

Por eso, ser un “fallen angel” no significa ser malo. Significa haber caído, haber conocido el lado difícil de la vida y haber cambiado sin dejar de ser uno mismo.

En resumen: no es una historia sobre una villana, sino sobre una caída, una transformación y la aceptación de uno mismo. 🪽🔥🌹

¿Qué significan y cómo son?

El nombre: La palabra ángel viene del griego ángelos y del hebreo malák, que significan exactamente "mensajero". 

Naturaleza espiritual: No tienen un cuerpo físico como los humanos, sino que son espíritus. Sin embargo, la Biblia muestra que pueden tomar forma humana visible cuando es necesario. 

Personalidad: Tienen inteligencia, emociones y la capacidad de decidir. La Biblia señala que la mayoría permanece obediente a Dios, pero un grupo se rebeló y se convirtió en demonios. 

Poder: Son mucho más fuertes e inteligentes que los seres humanos, aunque su conocimiento y poder siguen siendo limitados comparados con los de Dios. 

¿Cuál es su función?

Llevar mensajes: Anuncian planes divinos importantes, como ocurrió con el ángel Gabriel al hablar con María o Zacarías.

Proteger y guiar: Cuidan de los fieles en momentos de peligro o necesidad por mandato de Dios.

Alabar a Dios: Pasan su tiempo en el cielo glorificando al Creador sin descanso.

Ejecutar justicia: Actúan como instrumentos del juicio de Dios contra el mal.

Buenas, Dios los bendiga 😉

Los seres humanos son criaturas especiales creadas a imagen y semejanza de Dios, compuestas por un cuerpo físico y un componente espiritual. 

Creación y Naturaleza

A imagen de Dios: Los humanos reflejan las cualidades de Dios, como el amor, la justicia y la creatividad.

Origen dual: Dios formó el cuerpo físico del ser humano con el polvo de la tierra y sopló en él aliento de vida.

Tres dimensiones: La Biblia describe al ser humano integrado por espíritu, alma y cuerpo. El cuerpo conecta con el mundo físico, el alma comprende la mente y las emociones, y el espíritu permite la relación con Dios. 

Propósito y Rol

Mayordomía: Recibieron la autoridad y la tarea de cuidar, administrar y gobernar la creación de Dios de forma responsable.

Naturaleza relacional: Fueron diseñados para vivir en comunidad, relacionándose tanto con su Creador como con los demás seres humanos.

La caída del ser humano bíblicamente es el momento en que Adán y Eva desobedecieron a Dios en el Jardín del Edén, lo que introdujo el pecado y la muerte al mundo. Este relato se encuentra en el libro de Génesis, capítulo 3. 

El Relato en el Edén 

El mandato: Dios puso a Adán y Eva en un lugar perfecto y les dio libertad de comer de todo, excepto del árbol del conocimiento del bien y del mal.

La tentación: Una serpiente (asociada con Satanás) engañó a Eva al dudar de la palabra de Dios y sugerir que serían como Dios.

La desobediencia: Eva y Adán comieron el fruto prohibido de forma deliberada. 

Consecuencias Principales 

Ruptura espiritual: Se rompió la comunión directa y cercana que los humanos tenían con Dios, sintiendo vergüenza y culpa. 

Entrada del sufrimiento y la muerte: La maldición trajo dolor en el trabajo, dificultad en la crianza/parto y la mortalidad física para toda la humanidad. 

Naturaleza pecaminosa: Este acto afectó a toda la descendencia, heredando una tendencia hacia el pecado.  La naturaleza humana queda corrompida y afectada por una inclinación hacia el mal

La Promesa de Restauración

A pesar del castigo y la expulsión del Edén, la Biblia plantea desde ese mismo momento un plan divino de redención a través de Jesucristo para reconciliar a la humanidad con Dios. Todo esto lo dice la biblia 🙂‍↕️

Este plan se compone de etapas esenciales:

Las Etapas del Plan de Salvación 

La creación y el propósito: Dios creó al mundo y al ser humano en perfecta armonía, con el propósito de tener una relación cercana con él.

El problema del pecado: La humanidad se apartó de Dios mediante la desobediencia, introduciendo el pecado al mundo. Esto creó una separación entre Dios y el ser humano, cuya consecuencia es la muerte espiritual. 

La provisión en Jesucristo: Como las personas no pueden salvarse por sí mismas, Dios envió a Jesucristo. Jesús vivió sin pecado y pagó el precio de las faltas humanas al morir en la cruz.

La respuesta humana: La salvación se recibe por gracia mediante la fe en Jesucristo, el arrepentimiento sincero de los pecados y la aceptación de su sacrificio redentor. 

La restauración final: El plan culmina con la promesa de la vida eterna y la restauración plena de la comunión con Dios. 😊

text:
FALLEN ANGEL is essentially a story about love, temptation, losing yourself in someone, and eventually recognizing that the relationship isn't what you imagined it to be.
The “fallen angel” idea works as a metaphor: Jennie presents someone who initially seems almost pure, beautiful, or heavenly, but gets pulled into something complicated and emotionally destructive.
The storyline can be understood in a few stages:
1. ✨ The angelic beginning
At first, there's an almost dreamlike attraction. Everything feels beautiful and special, as though the other person is someone worth completely surrendering yourself to.
2. 🖤 Falling
The “fall” represents becoming emotionally attached and losing some of your independence. The relationship becomes increasingly complicated, with desire and vulnerability mixed together.
3. 🌑 Reality sets in
Eventually, the fantasy doesn't match reality. The person or relationship that seemed perfect has darker sides. The angel isn't simply “evil”—she's hurt, conflicted, and changed by what she's experienced.
4. 🪽 Becoming your own person
The important part is that being a “fallen angel” doesn't necessarily mean being ruined forever. It's more like falling from an idealized version of love and seeing things clearly.
So, rather than a literal story about an angel falling from heaven, it's better interpreted as an emotional metaphor for falling hard for someone and discovering the complicated reality behind that love.

text:
Watching the video for the second time made me think and interpret the whole song in a way that this is Jennie’s lament to her father.

The first part of the video where the girl says they can still fly and be free as can be makes me think that it is her mom talking to her, assuring her that they can still be happy without him. And seeing all the kids in this music video outside of a house burning down makes me think of kids without a home or without their parents present in their lives: fallen angels, but not in the biblical sense.

“Hey, can’t you stay?” Sounds like a desperate plea coming from a kid who sees her parent one foot out the door.

And all the frozen blue roses are what keeps Jennie’s home from burning down. Mama Kim ALWAYS gives Jennie blue roses for her birthday.

And the geese! They appeared many times. Geese symbolise teamwork, loyalty, and vigilance to protect their young, yet they always appear alone (the stuffed toy, and the shadow by the window) or moving away from each other (0:48) … They were watching Jennie floating, but they didn’t catch her! Geese fly in a V formation to share the workload and help weaker members travel further. In this MV, they did opposite of what they represent. And it’s just BRILLIANT!

The MV also evokes an uneasy/scary feeling right after the song ends, maybe it is to make us feel how scary the world is for kids without a home/family.

The last monologue breaks my heart… it appears to me that little Jennie is comforting the older Jennie. It seemed like she was considered a “thorn” when she was younger, yet her she is now, the world’s most beautiful flower.

Jennie has the mind of a great storyteller and sunburnkids did it justice.

PS. These are all my point of view/interpretation. You’re welcome to have a different view and scroll down.

text: Bananas are technically berries, while strawberries are not. Botanically speaking, a berry is a fruit that develops from a single ovary of a flower and contains seeds embedded within the flesh, which is exactly how bananas form. Strawberries, on the other hand, are considered “aggregate fruits” because they develop from multiple ovaries of a single flower, with each little seed-like speck (called an achene) on the outside being its own tiny fruit. Interestingly, this botanical definition of berries means that other fruits you wouldn’t expect—like kiwis, grapes, and even tomatoes—fit the true definition of a berry, while many of the fruits we commonly call berries, like raspberries and blackberries, technically don’t.

JENNIE devoured every aspect of this performance and left NO crumbs. The heavenly vocals, songwriting, music, gorgeous visuals, cinematography, styling, acting chops, storytelling and EVERYTHING ELSE… she really did THAT.

I absolutely LOVE the concept and the fact that JENNIE and the entire creative team went for something so different with this dark fantasy, dark fairy-tale, dreamy, surreal and horror-inspired aesthetic. It’s beautiful and magical one moment, and then suddenly eerie, unsettling and creepy the next—and I LOVE that contrast. 🖤🌹

Some of the surreal visuals were also giving me a little bit of It’s Okay to Not Be Okay vibes. Not necessarily because I think JENNIE was directly inspired by the drama, but because of that similar combination of dark fairy-tale imagery, surrealism, fantasy, psychological darkness and horror. That drama also used surreal effects and different animation styles to tell its story, so I definitely felt that connection here.

And speaking of the horror influences, I could be completely wrong, but I feel like you can see and maybe even feel inspiration from both old-school and modern horror, dark fantasy and supernatural/apocalyptic stories throughout the video. The different animation and visual styles, the creepy imagery, the cult-like atmosphere and especially that ending really got my imagination going.

Because THAT ENDING??? 😭

There are so many ways to interpret it. JENNIE could be the angel, she could be the Fallen Angel, or it could represent a transformation of some kind.

But part of me wonders if there's an even darker interpretation:

What if JENNIE isn't just the Fallen Angel who has fallen from heaven… what if she's the Fallen Angel who has ARRIVED? 🪽🔥

The burning house, the unsettling atmosphere, the little girl leading someone toward it, the angelic imagery and then JENNIE sitting there so calmly before pointing directly at the camera…

It almost feels like something out of a supernatural horror or apocalypse story where a dark supernatural being arrives and is somehow connected to the end of the world.

I'm NOT saying that's officially what the video means—I could be completely off—but as a personal interpretation, I LOVE the possibility that the Fallen Angel could represent something much darker… maybe even the beginning of an Apocalypse. 🔥🪽

And I LOVE that the MV leaves enough ambiguity for us to interpret it in different ways instead of explaining everything to us.

The message of the music video is also so meaningful and beautiful. I was genuinely in awe and honestly a little emotional watching it. The acting from the entire cast was amazing, including the little girl, whom I’m assuming represents a younger JENNIE or some part of her inner self.

And that quote toward the end??? 😭🌹

It absolutely made me emotional because it's so beautiful and relatable.

Huge kudos to JENNIE, the director, and the entire creative team behind this song and music video. They created something that feels like a gorgeous, haunting, surreal dark fairy tale, and I am SO here for it.

And of course, JENNIE looked absolutely gorgeous and was styled beautifully, as always. 🥹😍🖤🩷🔴💎🪽

I cannot WAIT to listen to the entire EP digitally and physically because I already know this project is going to be in HEAVY ROTATION.

JENNIE, you did THAT.

Another banger. Another masterpiece.

FALLEN ANGEL has officially arrived. 🪽🌹🔥

text:
My interpretation of the mv

1. The Fall (Loss of Innocence): Plunging into the pond and losing her wings symbolizes hitting rock bottom under the pressure of fame and being stripped of her untouchable status.

2. The Red Dress (Rebirth & Freedom): Shattering the doorless room shows that her mental barriers were fragile. Walking on the ground represents finding peace in reality rather than trying to fly.

3. Faceless Crowds (Hollow Success): Navigating dark rooms with blurred people symbolizes the isolation of celebrity life, showing that the surrounding crowd does not truly care about her.

4. The Spotlight (City Loneliness): Turning her back under a bright city spotlight represents being hyper-visible to the world yet utterly alone and disconnected.

5. Three Pictures (Love Overcomes Everything): The photos of couples—on a sofa, young, and in prison—prove that genuine love brings warmth and happiness, no matter how trapped or damaged you are.

6. Burning House (Childhood Dream): The little angel represents her childhood dream of true love. The burning house signifies letting her old, artificial life burn away to build a real home from the ashes.

A Jennie era a minha menos favorita do grupo, não me sentia tão conectada, mas dps do primeiro álbum solo dela (Ruby), eu me conectei com ela de uma forma que eu não sei explicar, sou uma pessoa que não sou de discutir na internet, mas o hate que ela vem tomando muito fez com que eu me apegasse mais ainda nela, fazendo com que eu me posicionasse na internet para defender ela dos hates desnecessários. A Jennie vem se mostrando ser uma artista completa, é incrível saber que ela entregou uns dos melhores álbuns do kpop, sendo o primeiro dela e logo após veio mostrando muito mais do q só músicas. As performances, as roupas, os clipes, as composições, os instrumentais, tudo tem um dedo dela! Hoje em dia eu me vejo muito apegada nela, tendo ela como a minha favorita por vários motivos, a Jennie é uma mulher tão esforçada e merece muito reconhecimento e muito mais fama, é uma artista que eu não tenho medo de acompanhar, é uma artista completa. A Jennie expressa os seus sentimentos, fazendo com que eu me sinta conectada, me toca muito. Eu tô chorando, eu sei que pode ser bobo, mas realmente esse clipe me deixou sensível e eu sinto muito por ela ser tão atacada, de forma assustadora! Só tenho a desejar tudo de bom pra ela e agradecer pelos trabalhos incríveis que ela vem mostrando. Te amo, Ninie❤️

1. Good video concept.
2. Good lyrics.
3. Good vocals, although there were a few unnecessary vocal effects that took away from her performance.

4. Strangely disjointed orchestration: very nice and appropriate at the beginning, sort of "meh" in the middle (and the guitar was a mess, just awful) but recovers at the end. Perhaps an effort to musically capture the concept of the fall of an angel? If so, the artistic risk did not pay off.
   Altogether, a good effort and a decent listen, but I do hope that the final version gets a re-mixed vocals line that takes out those effects and, if the guitar was intended to be like that, a re-recorded guitar that goes much harder on the fall.
